title: Environment Manager: Cancel button doesn't cancel — every edit and destructive action persists to disk immediately
existing_state: EnvironmentDialog presents classic Save/Cancel semantics (_btnSave/_btnCancel with DialogResult.OK/Cancel, EnvironmentDialog.cs:249-250, AcceptButton/CancelButton at 264-265), but nothing is actually staged. Every list selection change calls PersistCurrentEnvironmentDetails() (EnvironmentDialog.cs:403-414), which writes description, label color, variables, and vault-profile binding straight through EnvironmentService.UpdateEnvironmentDetails to config on disk (802-823) — and silently swallows any write failure (819-822). New/Duplicate/Rename/Delete/Import all execute immediately through the service (427, 449, 471, 499, 595). BtnSave_Click's only real effect is setting SelectedEnvironmentName so Form1 switches environments (639-643). A user who deletes an environment, fat-fingers a variable value, or imports over an existing environment and then clicks Cancel has still permanently committed all of it — the opposite of what the button promises.
recommendation: Pick one model and make the UI honest about it. Option A (preferred): stage edits in an in-memory working set (clone the environment list on open; route New/Duplicate/Rename/Delete/Import and detail edits against the clone) and commit everything in one EnvironmentService transaction on Save — mirroring how SettingsDialog batches its ~80 settings into a single _configService.Update (SettingsDialog.cs:2663). Option B (cheap): keep immediate-apply but remove the false affordance — rename Save to 'Switch & Close' and Cancel to 'Close', and add a small caption ('Changes are saved as you go').
user_benefit: Users can experiment safely in the environment manager and trust Cancel to mean cancel — today a misclick on Delete or a bad import is unrecoverable even after cancelling the dialog.

evidence.note: Save/Cancel buttons with DialogResult semantics implying a staged transaction
Selection change persists details to disk via EnvironmentService; exceptions swallowed
New/Rename/Delete/Import act immediately; Save only sets SelectedEnvironmentName
In-house precedent: SettingsDialog stages everything into one Update on Save

mockup_idea: EnvironmentDialog footer before (Save/Cancel) and after (single Close + 'changes apply immediately' hint, with 'Switch to selected' as the primary action) — or the transactional variant keeping Save/Cancel but with a pending-changes indicator.
